title: Probabilistic prefix compaction and shared KV pool for GPU memory optimization
creator: Lena Zhang
description:
Goal: Reduce peak GPU memory pressure from per-request prefix KV residency by introducing a compact, probabilistic deduplication layer and a shared on-device KV pool that allows safe reuse of identical or near-identical prefix KV fragments across concurrent requests and models.

Context: Prefix/prompt caching reduces compute by reusing previously-computed KV cache fragments, but naively storing full token-aligned KV shards per-request leads to high GPU memory usage at scale. Current efforts (fragment indexing, canonicalization) improve dedupe but retain deterministic metadata that is bulky. This ticket explores a complementary approach: fast content-derived compaction + probabilistic membership tests (Bloom/Golomb sketches) to cheaply identify candidate duplicate fragments, plus a shared KV pool with compact headers to enable cross-request sharing while preserving per-request isolation and correctness.

Key design goals:
- Substantially lower average GPU memory used for KV residency (target 20-35% reduction on mixed workload traces).
- Keep extra CPU overhead and latency minimal (probabilistic checks should be O(1) and amortized).
- Maintain deterministic decoding for model correctness: false positives must be handled via a safe verification path and not affect outputs.
- Support continuous batching and hot-path common-case (no verification required when confident).
- Interoperate with existing prefix canonicalization and fragment indexing (non-destructive).

Proposal summary:
1) Content fingerprinting (compact): compute a 64-bit rolling content hash per prefix fragment on CPU during request ingestion. Also compute a small sketch (Bloom filter with 3 hashes, 128-bit bitset) for token-level distribution summary for longer fragments.
2) Probabilistic index: maintain an in-memory per-GPU probabilistic index (shared across worker threads) mapping 64-bit fingerprints to compact pool handles. The index is optimized for insert/lookup and accepts a low false positive rate (~1e-4).
3) Shared KV pool layout (on-GPU): each pool entry stores compact header (64-bit fingerprint, 16-bit length bucket id, 16-bit refcount, 32-bit verification checksum pointer) + contiguous KV payload compressed with per-layer delta or 8-bit quantization. Payload alignment optimized for CUDA memory coalescing.
4) Verification path: on a probabilistic match, the worker performs a short verification: compare a 128-bit checksum (CRC64+xxhash) computed lazily on GPU or precomputed on CPU. If checksum matches, accept reuse. If not, fall back to per-request copy and consider inserting new pool entry. Verification is allowed to run asynchronously when used in batch mode; for single-request low-latency routes we run verification synchronously.
4b) False positives handling: never mutate model state based solely on a probabilistic match prior to verification. If verification fails, metrics increment and the request continues with local allocation.
5) Eviction & compaction: pool entries are organized by length buckets and LRU + size-aware eviction for long fragments. Periodic compaction merges pool entries that are byte-identical and removes stale entries (refcount 0 for > grace window).
6) Integration with continuous batching: when building a batch, the scheduler checks pool handles for each prefix; batch builder groups requests that share handles to enable KV pointer-sharing across the batch and avoid redundant copies. This reduces host<->device transfer bandwidth during batch assembly.

Acceptance criteria:
- Integration tests showing safe reuse across concurrent requests (no cross-request leakage).
- End-to-end benchmark: 25% median GPU KV memory reduction on our multi-tenant trace (>=15% on tail-heavy workloads) without measurable correctness regressions on downstream generation tests.
- Latency overhead of probabilistic lookup + verification should be <0.2ms p50 on hot-path; <1ms p99 for batch verification deferred paths.
- Automated stress test demonstrating bounded memory under sustained mixed workloads and safe eviction semantics.

Implementation plan (phased):
Phase 1 (spike, 2w): implement CPU-side fingerprinting + probabilistic index prototype, add instrumentation hooks, run offline trace replay to estimate dedupe effectiveness and false positive behavior. Deliverable: perf report + tuning parameters (hashers, bloom size).
Phase 2 (core impl, 4w): implement on-GPU pool layout and upload/download paths, verification checksum compute (GPU offload), thread-safe refcounting. Add integration with the batch assembler to use pool handles. Deliverable: feature behind runtime flag, unit & integration tests.
Phase 3 (canary, 2w): enable for dedicated canary customers and internal prod-like workloads with telemetry. Observe memory, latency, correctness metrics.
Phase 4 (rollout, 2w): expand canary to more clusters, implement adaptive eviction tuning, optimize sketch sizes, finalize dashboards and runbooks.

Telemetry & observability:
- Metrics: pool hit/miss rate, verification pass/fail, false-positive estimate, avg fragment size, refcount distribution, eviction rate, memory saved per-minute.
- Traces: attach fingerprint and verification result to request-level traces.
- Dashboards: per-cluster and per-model breakdowns showing memory savings and any verification failures correlated with model quality changes.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Bloom/hash collision causing frequent verification failures -> tune sketch parameters from spike data and make sketch size configurable per workload.
- Risk: CPU overhead for fingerprinting at high ingress rates -> offload hashing to a lightweight SIMD path or optional in-batch cooperative hashing.
- Risk: Memory fragmentation on GPU pool -> use length-bucketed slab allocator and periodic compaction.

Backward compatibility and config knobs:
- Feature gated behind runtime flag default-off for Hosted; opt-in for Dedicated.
- Configurable knobs: sketch size, fingerprint algorithm, verification mode (sync/async), length-bucket thresholds, pool size caps per-GPU.

Notes / links:
- Trace replay used for spike: s3://redwood-traces/prefix-reuse-2026-01 (internal).
- Design doc draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Probabilistic+Prefix+Compaction (internal).
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/11234 (WIP).

Work items (high level):
- CPU fingerprinting + sketch library (SIMD-optimized)
- Probabilistic index implementation (lock-free hashmap)
- On-GPU pool allocator & headers
- GPU checksum compute kernel + verification glue
- Batch assembler integration & pointer-sharing path
- Eviction, compaction and refcount lifecycle management
- Telemetry + dashboards + runbook updates

Edge cases:
- Very short prefixes (<=2 tokens): skip probabilistic path and use dedicated small-slot caching to avoid sketch overhead.
- Model parameter changes altering KV layout: attach model-version to pool entries and include in fingerprint namespace to avoid invalid reuse.

Estimated resource needs:
- 2 SDEs (runtime) + 1 infra SRE for rollout support + 0.5 PM for coordination during canary phase.

If approved, we will start the spike in 2026-W10 and aim for a canary rollout in runtime-1.22 canary clusters by the end of April.

2026-03-01 — Marco S. implemented a lock-free hashmap prototype; microbenchmarks show 0.05ms avg lookup on CPU core-local hot cache.
2026-03-07 — Integration test added: ensures verification failure never causes output divergence; test passed on x64 but found a dangling refcount bug on GPU allocator (fixed).
2026-03-12 — Canary gating proposal: default-off for hosted, opt-in flag for Dedicated controlled by org ID. Added telemetry for false-positive rate and verification latency.
